title: One token, two tools, one act.sub policy each
lede: Simulated: the agent's PingFederate token carries act = {"sub": "agent-client-example"}. The mock door evaluates one Cedar rule shape per tool. Simulate walks the scenario you picked; the measured run on a real tenant is shown separately below.

steps.title: The agent holds a PingFederate token
steps.what: act is an object {"sub": "agent-client-example"}; that is what the policy reads.
steps.why: If act were the text "{}" instead of an object it is believed to have no sub and so never to match (UNVERIFIED: simulated, not measured).

steps.title: The agent calls a tool
steps.what: tools/call with the token as a Bearer. The door checks sign-in first.
steps.why: No token is refused here, before any policy (in this mock; the real door's wording and checks were not measured).

steps.title: Each tool's Active policy is evaluated
steps.what: The policy on CountTool names the token's own agent; the policy on ListIndexTool names a different agent.
steps.why: Only Active policies are enforced; per the console documentation (not re-run here, UNVERIFIED) a Candidate is not.
